description:
Cycling in a leisurely fashion along London's network of cycle lanes, park routes, riverside pathways and smaller backstreets we'll see unique perspectives and hear entertaining tales of London past and present. There is something to discover around every corner, so be prepared to truly experience the city and create memories that will last for a lifetime.

We'll take in unique perspectives, and hear entertaining tales, of the Houses of Parliament, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey, Buckingham Palace, Trafalgar Square, the London Eye & St Paul's Cathedral.

What sets the tour apart from a more typical experience, though, are visits to an upside-down church, bomb shelters used in WWII, London's most exclusive private school, the world's smallest police station, the city's oldest wig store, a statue of Hodge, Dr Johnson's favourite cat, and the 'Banksy Tunnel' - London's largest legal graffiti zone.

When scheduled, we'll also avoid the crowds and get a front-row seat to the Changing of the Guard ceremony at our hidden spot, adjacent to Buckingham Palace; and we'll also include a refreshment break at Covent Garden for a bite to eat, a pint, or a chance to take in a street performance in front of St Paul's church.
Other things to note
Please call 07824 353274 if you're unable to find the meeting point, or running late. We do very much appreciate it you can arrive on time, though.
locationDescription: We'll explore hidden back streets and city squares, that take us back in time, magnificent architecture - both modern and venerable - and lesser known nooks and crannies missed out on by many a visitor.

Our bike tour of London was a wonderful experience in every way possible - great weather, decent bikes, interesting route, and best of all .... our fabulous guide, Patrick, who not only kept our group of ten (a good, manageable size) together and safe, particularly when we needed to navigate some busy areas of the city, but he also was a first-class storyteller who did a fantastic job of bringing the city's history to life. His reenactment of Admiral Horatio Nelson's final hours was Oscar -worthy, and he even serenaded us with a short Italian aria at the Opera House!!! A half hour into our trip and he already had learned everyone's name, and was very intent on keeping every person on the tour engaged and interested the entire time. It really was a great way to see the city and also get in a little fitness too!!!

If possible, I recommend you schedule your tour for the weekend, when the streets are less crowded and more enjoyable. As far as fitness level, this ride is pretty casual, but there are some rides up the hill that can be moderately challenging. I was glad that I brought water and sunscreen with me, and that the bicycles had baskets for my backpack. The stories Paul told were entertaining and historically interesting. Really enjoyed the singing too. This tour has been a wonderful highlight of my London trip so far.
